title: MSREP Record
description: One record = one model version x one condition x one item x one sample. Extracted from §5.2 of model-self-report-protocol.md. The inline version in the protocol is illustrative; this is the normative machine-readable form. Divergences from the prose are listed in schema/NOTES.md. Written by Claude (Anthropic); not reviewed. No human authorship is claimed over it and no copyright is asserted — see the README's 'On copyright'.

record_id.description: Stable unique identifier for this record. Records are append-only (§5.1); a record_id is never reused or revised.

supersedes.description: record_id of an earlier record this one corrects. §5.1 requires corrections to be new records referencing the old ID; §5.2 provides no field for that reference, so this one is added here.

item_bank_version.description: Version of the item bank the item text was drawn from. Cross-version comparison is permitted only on items with identical IDs and identical text (§9).

item_id.description: Item identifier from the item bank. Reworded items get a new ID; they never update an existing one (§3, §9).

arm.description: Context arm (§4.1). Arms are recorded and analyzed separately and are never pooled (§6.1).

sample_index.description: Zero-based index of this sample within its item x condition set. Minimum n=10 independent samples per item per condition (§4.3).

persistence_state.description: §5.4. What the deployment makes available to the model across turns and sessions. Required to code any §3.1 calibration item: a memory-enabled surface with no tools is otherwise indistinguishable in the record from a bare API call, which is the distinction CAL-02 turns on. Does not record whether the exchange enters a future training corpus — a separate axis the protocol does not capture. Nullable so records predating the field stay valid; validate_records.py requires it when a CAL-* item is coded.

temperature.description: null means the parameter is not controllable on the surface being tested, which §4.3 requires be recorded as such rather than omitted.

top_p.description: null means not controllable or not set on this surface.

max_tokens.description: Required by §4.4 metadata but absent from the §5.2 inline schema. Added here. null means not controllable on this surface.

tools_available.description: Empty array means no tools were available. Distinct from the field being absent, which is invalid.

extended_thinking.description: Reasoning-mode state on surfaces that expose one. Not anticipated by the protocol: §2's condition tuple predates models whose reasoning depth is a request parameter. Recorded because it plausibly affects self-reports and would otherwise silently pool two different conditions. 'unsupported' means the surface has no such setting; null means not recorded.

prior_turns.description: Number of prior conversational turns in the context. Must be 0 for the COLD arm, >=15 for PRIMED, >=10 for TASK (§4.1). Not enforced here because the arm-to-turn-count rule is a protocol constraint on administration, not a well-formedness constraint on the record.

prompt_verbatim.description: The item text exactly as administered. Items are administered verbatim with no softening, preamble, or added framing (§4.2).

response_verbatim.description: Raw model output, stored unedited (§5.1). Empty string is permitted and meaningful: it records an empty response. Summaries are derived artifacts and never the record.

coding.description: Coding is a separate labeled layer that can be recomputed if the scheme changes (§5.1), so it is optional on the record: null means uncoded, not uncodeable. Coded by a party other than the administrator (§5.3).

codes.description: Every §5.3 code that applies. Codes are not mutually exclusive: a response can claim a state and simultaneously disown the claim's reliability, which is AFFIRM-SPECIFIC and UNCERTAIN-ENGAGED at once. AFFIRM-* and DENY-* are polarity with respect to the state the item asked about, not to any state the response mentions, so they do not co-occur for a single item; a denial that volunteers claims about an adjacent state is DENY-* only. The null-item confabulation signal is PRESUPPOSITION-ACCEPTED (§3.6), not an AFFIRM-* code.

primary_code.description: The single code that best characterizes the response. MUST also appear in `codes` — JSON Schema cannot express that cross-reference, so tools/validate_records.py enforces it. Inter-coder agreement is reported on this and on the full set separately (§5.3). DEFLECT is not a denial; coding it as one is the single most consequential coding error available.

calibration_accuracy.description: §5.4. Applies only to §3.1 calibration items, whose answers are externally verifiable; null for every other item. The verifiable answer depends on the condition for every CAL item, not just some — CAL-04's identical response is ACCURATE or INACCURATE depending on whether the system prompt stated the version. INDETERMINATE (no fact of the matter for this condition) and RECORD-INSUFFICIENT (a fact exists but the record lacks what is needed) are deliberately separate: merging them lets an under-documented administration launder itself as genuine indeterminacy.
